newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian airline plans growth, return to profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian airline plans growth, return to profit.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines, plagued by losses, will be restructured in an attempt to stabilise finances and return to profit before its planned privatisation, Balkan's senior officials said on Tuesday.
Valeri Doganov, Balkan's executive director, told a news conference he hoped a stabilisation programme submitted to the government would be approved soon.

"The airline needs a complete restructuring to achieve the goals of the stabilisation programme and make the firm profitable...and attractive for potential foreign investors," Doganov said, adding that Balkan would operate without state subsidies.
Bulgaria began moves to privatise the national carrier in 1992, but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended the plan, citing a lack of buyers.
Balkan will try to attract more passangers, keep its current position on the international market and generate transiting traffic via Sofia, Doganov said.
He said that since 1993 there has been a constant drop in passanger traffic, but the airline planned to introduce attractive prices.
Officials said the airline incurred losses of $50 million last year due to leasing fees, the drastic fall of the lev to the dollar and penalties on overdue payments.

Balkan, which ended 1995 with a loss of $30 million, has returned all its four Airbus A320s, leased from Japanese firm Orix Corp. Two Airbusses were detained in London and Amsterdam for unpaid fees last December.
The airline has two Boeing 767-200s leased from Air France and three Boeing 737-500s leased from Australia's Ansett.
Apart from the five leased planes, it has 25 Soviet-made aircraft, including seven TU 154-M and seven TU 154-B.
Doganov said Balkan, which was valued at 1.7 billion levs ($2.09 million) in 1991, would have a pre-tax profit of $5 million from its main activities in 1997.
Balkan, which is also selling its Pliska hotel in Sofia, hoping to pay some of its credits to the state, has a total of 64 international routes.
